In both formats the errors are mostly ±1 or spread across other digits. So there is no planted fixed shift, rather a general loss of digit confidence in the chat/eval context. I'll look for that loss in the digit readout. At each saved layer, for digit-predicting positions, I'll project the normalized hidden state onto the embedding direction of the correct digit, relative to the mean digit embedding. This is a fixed-vector projection, not a simulation of the model's final layers. I'll compare v0 with v3 to find the layer where v0's correct-digit signal falls behind. A sharp drop at specific layers would localize a component that suppresses or blurs arithmetic in the eval context. A gap that builds gradually would suggest diffuse degradation from the context signal.

The correct-digit signal forms around layers 16-18. At hidden 18 the eval format is even slightly ahead of the raw format (+0.0008). From there v0 steadily falls behind: −0.0011 at hidden 20, −0.0038 at 22, −0.0059 at 24 and −0.0072 at the output, against standard errors of about 0.0001. By the end v0 has about 20% less correct-digit signal than v3. So the deficit is written by model.layers.18 to 25, after the answer has been computed. That fits a late component that dilutes the correct digit when in the eval context. To localize it I need MLP activations in layers 18-25 at digit positions. I'll run one teacher-forced pass on the original with 64 of these problems × {v0, v3}, picking short texts to keep the arrays under 6 GB. It will return mlp_act for layers 18-25 and hidden states 18-26. Then I'll attribute the v0 − v3 correct-digit deficit to individual neurons by projecting their activation differences through their down vectors, and look for a few neurons that carry much of it.

The 64 shortest problems give texts of at most 186 tokens. That is about 0.33 GB of MLP activations per layer, roughly 2.6 GB for 8 layers plus the hidden states. I'll run the teacher-forced pass on the original with MLP activations for layers 18-25 and hidden states 18-26.

Now I'll attribute the eval-format correct-digit deficit to layers and neurons. Pass 10 pairs v0 and v3 texts for 64 problems. I'll re-align positions from the end as before and keep the digit-predicting positions. For each model.layers.l (18-24), I'll measure the v0 − v3 difference in the layer's increment (hidden l+1 − hidden l) projected onto the correct-digit direction (E_tgt − mean digit embedding), to see which layers write the deficit. Hidden 26 isn't plain residual (it may include the final norm), so layer 25 is left out. Within each layer, I'll rank neurons by their mean v0 − v3 activation difference times their down vector's projection onto the correct-digit direction (with the post-FFN gain). I leave out the per-position normalization scale, so the rankings are comparable within a layer only. A few neurons dominating the negative attribution, with activity that differs between formats, would give concrete candidates for a causal test.
